summary: Source-based expansion of the enhanced derived-category layer. E0: stable ∞-categories, suspension, exact functors and the triangulated homotopy category (HA §§1.1.1–1.1.4) and the dg nerve with its Dold–Kan comparison (HA §1.3.1). E1: the injective model structure and the derived ∞-category of a Grothendieck abelian category (HA §1.3.5) and functorial K-injective and K-flat resolutions for sheaves of modules (Stacks Project chapters 13, 19, 21). E2: replete topoi, left completion, Postnikov convergence criteria and hypercover descent (Bhatt–Scholze §§3.1–3.3). E3: relative left Kan extensions with existence, uniqueness and adjunction (HTT §4.3.2), fibre-slice cofinality (HTT Lemma 4.3.3.9), enhanced derived categories of ringed topoi (Liu–Zheng arXiv v2 §2 = v4 §§3.1–3.2), partial adjoints, and the adjoint functor theorem statements as used in Scholze's ECD §§17, 22–23, 26. E4: derived I-completion of sheaves and reconstruction from the coefficients R/mⁿ (Bhatt–Scholze §§3.4–3.5), applying the generic completion owned by DerivedDeRhamCohomology DD.1. E5 sub-stages: ∞-operads and symmetric monoidal ∞-categories (HA §§2.0–2.1), idempotent completion (HTT §5.1.4), Ind-completion (HTT §5.3.5, HA 1.1.3.6, 4.8.1.14), sifted colimits and P_Σ (HTT §5.5.8) and animated rings (Bhatt–Lurie, Appendix A). Recorded ordering problems: Kan-extension uniqueness is used by E0 and E5:abstract before E3, and several coherence steps in ECD are asserted without proof.

nodes.title: Relative left Kan extensions along a full subcategory (pointwise definition and invariance)
nodes.statement: Let C⁰ ⊆ C be a full subcategory of an ∞-category, p: D → D′ an inner fibration and F: C → D a functor lying over a given C → D′, with F₀ = F|C⁰. Put C⁰_{/C} = C_{/C} ×_C C⁰. A diagram q̄: K^▷ → D is a p-colimit of q = q̄|K if D_{q̄/} → D_{q/} ×_{D′_{pq/}} D′_{pq̄/} is a trivial fibration. F is a p-left Kan extension of F₀ at C ∈ C if the induced diagram (C⁰_{/C})^▷ → D exhibits F(C) as a p-colimit, and a p-left Kan extension if this holds at every C; for D′ = Δ⁰ this is the absolute pointwise left Kan extension. The condition holds automatically at objects of C⁰, and is invariant under equivalences C ≃ C′ of objects, under equivalences F ≃ F′ of functors and under replacing the whole square by a categorically equivalent one.
hypotheses: C⁰ ⊆ C full. An inner fibration p suffices for the definition and for Lemmas 4.3.2.5–4.3.2.6; existence, transitivity, uniqueness and adjunction statements require p to be a categorical fibration.
Over a point a p-colimit is an ordinary colimit (an initial object of the undercategory); an edge is a p-colimit of its source iff it is p-coCartesian (Example 4.3.1.4).
proofSteps: Remark 4.3.2.3: for C ∈ C⁰, id_C is final in C⁰_{/C}, so {id_C} → C⁰_{/C} is cofinal and the condition reduces to a trivial one (cofinality of a final object and Example 4.3.1.4 are used without citation).
Example 4.3.2.4: for C = K^▷ and C⁰ = K, p-left Kan extensions are exactly p-colimit diagrams (definition and Remark 4.3.2.3).
Lemma 4.3.2.5: for an equivalence f: C → C′ the maps C⁰_{/C} ← C⁰_{/f} → C⁰_{/C′} are trivial fibrations, hence cofinal; conclude with Propositions 4.3.1.5 and 4.3.1.7.

Lemma 4.3.2.6: invariance under equivalent functors by Proposition 4.3.1.5, and under a ladder of categorical equivalences by Proposition 4.3.1.6 applied pointwise, Proposition 1.2.9.3 for slices and essential surjectivity.

nodes.title: Existence of relative left Kan extensions: pointwise criterion and the coCartesian case
nodes.statement: Let C⁰ ⊆ C be full, p: D → D′ a categorical fibration, G: C → D′ and F₀: C⁰ → D over G|C⁰. (Lemma 4.3.2.13) A p-left Kan extension F of F₀ over G exists iff for every C ∈ C the diagram C⁰_{/C} → D admits a p-colimit compatible with (C⁰_{/C})^▷ → C → D′. (Lemma 4.3.2.7) If F is a p-left Kan extension of F₀, then D_{F/} → D′_{pF/} ×_{D′_{pF₀/}} D_{F₀/} is a trivial fibration, identifying p-colimits of F and of F₀. (Proposition 4.3.2.8) For full C⁰ ⊆ C¹ ⊆ C with F|C¹ a p-left Kan extension of F|C⁰, F is a p-left Kan extension of F|C¹ iff it is one of F|C⁰. (Corollary 4.3.2.14) If p: D → E is a coCartesian fibration whose fibres admit small colimits preserved by the transition functors, and C is small, then every F₀ admits a left Kan extension relative to p.
hypotheses: p a categorical fibration (used in the degenerate-simplex steps); C⁰ ⊆ C full; the relative colimits lie over the given base functor G.
Corollary 4.3.2.14 additionally needs C small, small colimits in the fibres, colimit-preserving transition functors and p genuinely coCartesian; Lemma 4.3.2.13 has no size hypothesis.
Fibrewise colimits become relative colimits by Proposition 4.3.1.10 (locally coCartesian fibrations) and Corollary 4.3.1.11 (coCartesian fibrations).
proofSteps: Lemma 4.3.2.7: filter C by adding the simplices σ with σ(0) ∉ C⁰ in order of dimension; at limit stages use inverse limits of trivial fibrations; for nondegenerate σ reduce to lifting ∂Δ^{n+m+1} ⊆ Δ^{n+m+1} against D_{g₀/} → D′_{pg₀/}, whose initial vertex is p-initial by the Kan extension hypothesis; for degenerate σ prove the inclusion of filtration stages is a categorical equivalence by writing a subcomplex of C⁰_{/σ} as a colimit over an index category with a final object (no labels cited).

nodes.title: Uniqueness of left Kan extensions as a trivial fibration and the adjunction i_! ⊣ i^*
nodes.statement: Let C⁰ ⊆ C be full and p: D → D′ a categorical fibration. Let K ⊆ Map_{D′}(C, D) be spanned by the p-left Kan extensions and K⁰ ⊆ Map_{D′}(C⁰, D) by those F₀ for which every C⁰_{/C} → D has a p-colimit over the given map. Then restriction K → K⁰ is a trivial fibration (Proposition 4.3.2.15). If every F₀ admits a p-left Kan extension, then i^*: Map_{D′}(C, D) → Map_{D′}(C⁰, D) has a section i_! whose essential image is exactly the p-left Kan extensions, the sections forming a contractible space (Corollary 4.3.2.16), and i_! is left adjoint to i^* (Proposition 4.3.2.17).

nodes.title: Fibrewise left Kan extensions over coCartesian fibrations and fibre-slice cofinality
nodes.statement: (HTT Lemma 4.3.3.9) Let p: C → E and q: C⁰ → E be coCartesian fibrations, i: C⁰ ⊆ C a full subcategory carrying q-coCartesian morphisms to p-coCartesian morphisms, and F: C → D. Then F is a left Kan extension of F|C⁰ iff for each E ∈ E the fibre restriction F_E: C_E → D is a left Kan extension of F_E|C⁰_E. The proof shows that for C over E the inclusion of the fibre slice (C⁰_E)_{/C} ⊆ C⁰_{/C} is right anodyne, hence cofinal, so the pointwise colimits may be computed on the fibre. HTT proves this only for absolute Kan extensions and explicitly does not develop the relative theory. ECD Lemma 22.16 uses the same pattern for its relative Kan extension over Δ, asserting the cofinality without an HTT label, and ECD Lemma 22.17 derives preservation of coCartesian edges from Lemma 22.16 and base change (Proposition 22.15); no general HTT criterion for preservation of coCartesian edges was found.
hypotheses: p and q coCartesian fibrations and i preserving coCartesian morphisms; absolute Kan extensions only in HTT 4.3.3.9 (Proposition 4.3.3.10, a version for a general δ over S preserving coCartesian edges, was read as a statement only).
The relative version over a base D′ needed by ECD §22 is not written in HTT and must be proved from §4.3.2 and this cofinality argument.

nodes.title: Enhanced derived categories for diagrams of ringed topoi with enough points (Liu–Zheng)
nodes.statement: Let RingedPTopos be the (2,1)-category of ringed topoi, in a fixed universe, with enough points. For such (X, O_X) there is a combinatorial model structure on Ch(Mod(X, O_X)) whose cofibrations are the monomorphisms with dg-flat cokernel, fibrations the epimorphisms with dg-cotorsion kernel and weak equivalences the quasi-isomorphisms; it is monoidal and (f^*, f_*) is a Quillen adjunction. Liu–Zheng construct a lax Cartesian structure T: N(RingedPTopos^op)^⨿ → Cat_∞ and T^⊗: N(RingedPTopos^op) → CAlg(Cat_∞)^L_{pr,st,cl}, sending (X, O_X) to its derived ∞-category D(X), presentable, stable and closed symmetric monoidal, a morphism to the symmetric monoidal left adjoint f^*, and small coproducts to products. Precomposing with the nerve of a diagram of ringed topoi gives the coherent diagram of derived ∞-categories and pullbacks used by ECD §22; for ringed diagrams (X, (Ξ, Λ)) one gets D(X, (Ξ, Λ)), and for constant rings D(X, (Ξ, Λ_Ξ)) ≃ Fun(N(Ξ^op), D(X, Λ)). Localization squares are left adjointable (Beck–Chevalley for j_!), and for perfect π the f^*/π^* square is right adjointable. ECD cites this as '[LZ14, Section 2]', which is §2 of arXiv v2 and §§3.1–3.2 of v4.

nodes.title: Stable ∞-categories, suspension, exact functors and the triangulated homotopy category
nodes.statement: An ∞-category C is stable if it has a zero object, every morphism admits a fibre and a cofibre, and a triangle is a fibre sequence iff it is a cofibre sequence (HA Definition 1.1.1.9). For stable C the functors Σ and Ω, defined through pushout and pullback squares with zero corners, are mutually inverse equivalences. If C is pointed, admits cofibres and Σ is an equivalence, then hC is additive (Lemma 1.1.2.9) and the shift [1] with the distinguished triangles of Definition 1.1.2.11 makes hC triangulated (Theorem 1.1.2.14); these hypotheses are equivalent to stability (Remark 1.1.2.15). A pointed C is stable iff it has finite limits and colimits and pushout squares coincide with pullback squares (Proposition 1.1.3.4). A functor between stable ∞-categories is left exact iff right exact iff exact (Proposition 1.1.4.1).
hypotheses: Transposing a square changes the classified map by a sign (Lemma 1.1.2.10), and the third map in Lemma 1.1.2.13 is −h′; the comparison of these signs with the cochain-complex cone convention is not in the parts read.

nodes.title: The differential graded nerve, its homotopy category and the Dold–Kan comparison
nodes.statement: For a dg category C over a commutative ring k (HA Definition 1.3.1.1), the dg nerve N_dg(C) has as n-simplices families of objects X₀, …, X_n and elements f_I ∈ Map(X_{min I}, X_{max I}) of degree determined by |I|, subject to the differential identity (1.1), with faces and degeneracies given by restriction, identities or zero (Construction 1.3.1.6). N_dg(C) is an ∞-category (Proposition 1.3.1.10); its homotopy category is canonically hC, where Hom_hC = H₀Map (Remark 1.3.1.11); and its mapping spaces are Hom^R(X, Y) ≅ DK(τ_{≥0}Map(X, Y)) (Remark 1.3.1.12). Truncating mapping complexes and applying Dold–Kan with the Alexander–Whitney map gives a fibrant simplicial category C_Δ and a map θ: N(C_Δ) → N_dg(C) that is an equivalence of ∞-categories (Constructions 1.3.1.13, 1.3.1.16, Proposition 1.3.1.17). For an additive category A, N_dg(Ch(A)) is stable with Σ the shift (Proposition 1.3.2.10).
hypotheses: HA grades complexes homologically; the reader notes that the degree bookkeeping in the proof of Proposition 1.3.1.10 is shifted by one relative to Construction 1.3.1.6, so degrees must be fixed against the construction.
Hom^R is the right mapping space of HTT §1.2.2; the comparison uses HTT 2.2.2.7, 2.2.2.9 and 2.2.2.13 (statements only).
proofSteps: Proposition 1.3.1.10: an inner horn determines all f_I except f_{[n]} and f_{[n]∖j}; put f_{[n]} = 0 and solve the differential identity for f_{[n]∖j} explicitly (no results cited).
Remark 1.3.1.11: hC → hN_dg(C) is bijective on objects and surjective on morphisms (Remark 1.3.1.9), and Example 1.3.1.8 identifies the relation on morphisms with homology.
Remark 1.3.1.12: simplices of Hom^R are chain maps N_*(ZΔⁿ) → Map(X, Y) after a sign change, identified with the Dold–Kan construction by Lemma 1.2.3.12.

nodes.title: The injective model structure and the derived ∞-category D(A) of a Grothendieck abelian category
nodes.statement: Let A be a Grothendieck abelian category, i.e. presentable with monomorphisms closed under small filtered colimits (HA Definition 1.3.5.1). Ch(A) has a left proper combinatorial model structure whose cofibrations are the degreewise monomorphisms and weak equivalences the quasi-isomorphisms (Proposition 1.3.5.3); it is not a simplicial model category (Warning 1.3.5.4). Fibrant complexes have injective terms, and complexes of injectives that vanish in sufficiently large homological degrees are fibrant (Proposition 1.3.5.6). D(A) is the dg nerve of the fibrant complexes (Definition 1.3.5.8). It is stable (Proposition 1.3.5.9), a localization of N_dg(Ch(A)) (Proposition 1.3.5.13), equivalent to the underlying ∞-category N(Ch(A))[W⁻¹] (Proposition 1.3.5.15), and presentable with an accessible right complete t-structure compatible with filtered colimits whose heart is A (Propositions 1.3.5.18, 1.3.5.21). D(A) is generally not left complete (Warning 1.3.5.22).
hypotheses: A Grothendieck in HA's sense; its equivalence with the Stacks definition (AB5 with a generator, Definition 19.10.1) is not stated in either source read.

nodes.title: Functorial K-injective resolutions in Grothendieck abelian categories and K-flat resolutions of sheaves of modules
nodes.statement: (Stacks Theorem 19.12.6) In a Grothendieck abelian category (AB5 with a generator) every complex M has a functorial quasi-isomorphism M → I, injective in each degree, with I K-injective and termwise injective. A complex I is K-injective if Hom_K(M, I) = 0 for all acyclic M (Definition 13.31.1); equivalently Hom_K(−, I) inverts quasi-isomorphisms, and then Hom_K(N, I) = Hom_D(N, I) (Lemma 13.31.2). Bounded below complexes of injectives are K-injective (Lemma 13.31.4), and when K-injective resolutions exist, right derived functors exist on unbounded derived categories and are computed on K-injectives (Lemma 13.31.7). For a ringed site, Mod(O) is Grothendieck (Tag 07A5), so RΓ and Rf_* exist on unbounded complexes. Bounded above complexes of flat modules are K-flat (Definition 21.17.2, Lemma 21.17.8); every complex receives a termwise surjective quasi-isomorphism from a K-flat complex with flat terms (Lemma 21.17.11, existence only), which defines − ⊗^L F independently of choices (Definition 21.17.13). Lf^* is computed on K-flat complexes with flat terms (Lemma 21.18.2), Lf^* ⊣ Rf_* on unbounded derived categories (Lemma 21.19.1), and f_* preserves K-injectives when f is flat (Lemma 21.20.10).

nodes.title: Replete topoi: exactness of countable products and of limits of towers of surjections
nodes.statement: A topos X is replete if surjections are closed under sequential limits: for every tower F_{n+1} → F_n of surjections, lim F → F_n is surjective (Bhatt–Scholze Definition 3.1.1). Slices of replete topoi are replete, and repleteness can be checked after a surjection X → 1 (Lemmas 3.1.2–3.1.3). Sets, presheaf topoi and the fpqc topos are replete, while Shv(Spec k_ét) is replete iff k̄/k is finite (Examples 3.1.4, 3.1.5, 3.1.7). In a replete topos, a map of towers whose relative maps are surjective has surjective limit map (Lemma 3.1.8); countable products are exact (Proposition 3.1.9); for a tower of abelian sheaves with surjective transitions lim ≃ R lim (Proposition 3.1.10); and N^op-indexed limits have cohomological dimension 1 (Proposition 3.1.11). Locally weakly contractible topoi are replete (Proposition 3.2.3(1)).
hypotheses: Repleteness is a sequential condition; the cofiltered analogue leads to an empty theory (Remark 3.1.6).
The Zariski, étale, Nisnevich, smooth and fppf topoi of most schemes are not replete (discussion after Remark 3.1.6), so generic lemmas must not assume repleteness.
proofSteps: Lemma 3.1.8: set X₀ = X ×_{G₀} F₀ and X_{n+1} = X_n ×_{F_n ×_{G_n} G_{n+1}} F_{n+1}, a tower of surjections; lim X_n → X is surjective by repleteness, which gives the lift.
Proposition 3.1.9: write ∏ f_n as lim_n ∏_{i<n} f_i and apply Lemma 3.1.8.
Proposition 3.1.10: by 3.1.9 there is a triangle R lim F → ∏ F_n → ∏ F_n with second map t − id; the partial-product maps satisfy the hypotheses of Lemma 3.1.8, so t − id is surjective.
Proposition 3.1.11: combine the triangle, Proposition 3.1.9 and long exact sequences to get R lim F_n ∈ D^{[0,1]}.
Proposition 3.2.3(1): surjectivity can be tested on weakly contractible objects, over which surjections have sections.
acceptance: Example 3.1.5: if the separable closure of k is infinite over k, an infinite tower of finite separable extensions gives surjections with empty limit.
Postnikov convergence in the hypercomplete ∞-topos of a replete topos is left open (Question 3.1.12); do not assume it.

nodes.title: Left completion, left completeness of replete topoi and the cohomological-dimension criterion
nodes.statement: For any topos X, the left completion D̂(X) ⊂ D(X^N) consists of systems {K_n} with K_n ∈ D^{≥−n} and τ^{≥−n}K_{n+1} ≃ K_n, and D(X) is left-complete if τ: K ↦ {τ^{≥−n}K} is an equivalence (Definition 3.3.1). R lim: D̂(X) → D(X) is right adjoint to τ, so if D(X) is left-complete then K ≃ R lim τ^{≥−n}K (Lemma 3.3.2). If X is replete, D(X) is left-complete (Proposition 3.3.3). Left completeness fails for the topos of finite ∏Z_p-sets (Example 3.3.4), and the argument applies to Spec(k)_ét when classes α_n of unbounded orders exist (Remark 3.3.5). For any topos, if Γ(U, −) is exact then RΓ(U, K) ≃ R lim RΓ(U, τ^{≥−n}K) (Proposition 3.3.7(1)); if the cohomology sheaves have cohomological dimension at most d locally on X, D(X) is left-complete (Proposition 3.3.7(2), proved only by citing Stacks Tag 0719).
hypotheses: Definition 3.3.1, Lemma 3.3.2 and Proposition 3.3.7(1) hold in any topos; Proposition 3.3.3 needs repleteness.

Proposition 3.3.7(2) as printed mixes a hypothesis on one K with a conclusion for all of D(X) and does not define 'locally'; later uses in Bhatt–Scholze assume uniform bounds (condition (A) on p. 40; p. 48).
proofSteps: Lemma 3.3.2: RHom(K, R lim L_n) ≃ R lim RHom(τ^{≥−n}K, L_n), called formal; the equalizer sequence for Hom in Ab(X^N) becomes a triangle for K-injective targets ('one can check'); on D̂, RHom(F_{n+1}, G_n) = RHom(F_n, G_n).
Proposition 3.3.3, full faithfulness: by 3.3.2 it suffices that K ≃ R lim τ^{≥−n}K; ∏ τ^{≥−n}I is the derived product (3.1.9) and t − id is surjective in each degree as in 3.1.10.

Proposition 3.3.3, essential surjectivity: K-injective systems {I_n} have degreewise surjective transitions (asserted); H^i commutes with ∏ (3.1.9) and H^i(t − id) is split surjective with the expected kernel.
Example 3.3.4: for K = ⊕ Z/pⁿ[n], H⁰p^*K = 0, while H⁰p^*K̂ contains a nonzero class built from classes α_n ∈ Hⁿ(Z_pⁿ, Z/pⁿ) of exact order pⁿ via a transfer argument, so K → K̂ has no section.

The bounded-below parts of the first and third statements do not use repleteness; the unbounded case uses repleteness of X and of every X_n.

nodes.title: Derived I-completion for sheaves of rings in a replete topos
nodes.statement: Let X be a replete topos, R a sheaf of rings and I ⊂ R a locally finitely generated ideal; for a local section x put T(K, x) = R lim(⋯ → K → K) with transition maps multiplication by x. K ∈ D(X, R) is derived I-complete if T(K|_U, x) = 0 for all local sections x of I (Definition 3.4.1). Completeness can be tested on local generators and is equivalent to K ≃ R lim(K → K) along multiplication by xⁿ, and to K|_U ≃ R lim(K ⊗^L_{Z[x]} Z[x]/(x₁ⁿ, …, x_rⁿ)) (Lemma 3.4.12). K is derived complete iff each H^i(K) is (Proposition 3.4.4). The inclusion D_comp(X, R) ⊆ D(X, R) has a left adjoint K ↦ K̂ (Lemma 3.4.9), giving the completed tensor product K ⊗̂ L = (K ⊗^L L)^ and RHom_R(K, L) complete for complete L (Definition 3.4.10, Lemma 3.4.11). Classically complete modules are derived complete (Lemma 3.4.13); a module is classically complete iff it is I-adically separated and derived complete (Proposition 3.4.2); derived complete modules form a Serre subcategory (Lemma 3.4.14).
hypotheses: Repleteness is used in 3.4.2 (Milnor sequence), 3.4.4 (left completeness), 3.4.13–3.4.14 (lim = R lim and cohomological dimension of R lim) and, through descent, in 3.4.9.
The generic module-level derived completion is owned by DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.1; this node is its sheaf-level application in a replete topos, as E4's stage text requires.

Lemma 3.4.9: with global generators set F_{i+1}K = cone(T(F_iK, x_{i+1}) → F_iK) ≃ R lim(F_iK ⊗^L Z[x]/(xⁿ)); induction with 3.4.7–3.4.8 shows K → F_rK is the left adjoint; in general pass to a hypercover and use cohomological descent.

nodes.title: Noetherian derived completion and reconstruction from the coefficients R/mⁿ
nodes.statement: Let X be replete, R a noetherian ring and m ⊂ R an ideal, viewed as constant sheaves. nodes.title: ∞-operads, symmetric monoidal ∞-categories, commutative algebras and monoidal functors
nodes.statement: Fin_* has objects ⟨n⟩ = {*, 1, …, n} and base-point-preserving maps; a map is inert if each preimage of a non-base point has exactly one element, and active if the preimage of the base point is the base point (HA Notation 2.0.0.2, Definitions 2.1.1.8, 2.1.2.1). An ∞-operad is a functor p: O^⊗ → N(Fin_*) of ∞-categories such that inert morphisms have p-coCartesian lifts, mapping spaces over a map f decompose as the product over the ρ^i ∘ f (Segal condition), and any objects C₁, …, C_n over ⟨1⟩ receive coCartesian maps over the ρ^i from an object over ⟨n⟩ (Definition 2.1.1.10). A symmetric monoidal ∞-category is a coCartesian fibration C^⊗ → N(Fin_*) whose functors ρ^i_! induce C^⊗_⟨n⟩ ≃ (C^⊗_⟨1⟩)^n (Definition 2.0.0.7). Maps of ∞-operads preserve inert morphisms (Definition 2.1.2.7); CAlg(C) consists of the ∞-operad maps from N(Fin_*) to C^⊗ over N(Fin_*) (Definition 2.1.3.1); symmetric monoidal functors are ∞-operad maps preserving coCartesian morphisms (Definition 2.1.3.7). For an ∞-operad O^⊗ and a coCartesian fibration C^⊗ → O^⊗, C^⊗ is an ∞-operad iff the inert maps give C^⊗_T ≃ ∏ C^⊗_{T_i} (Proposition 2.1.2.12). The symmetric monoidal structure on CAlg(C) is coCartesian, so CAlg(C) has finite coproducts (Proposition 3.2.4.7, Corollary 3.2.4.8).

The nerve of an ordinary symmetric monoidal category is a symmetric monoidal ∞-category whose commutative algebras are the classical ones (Examples 2.1.2.21, 2.1.3.3), stated without written proofs.

nodes.title: Idempotent completion, its universal property and stability of the completion
nodes.statement: A functor f: C → D exhibits D as an idempotent completion of C if D is idempotent complete, f is fully faithful and every object of D is a retract of some f(C) (HTT Definition 5.1.4.1). Every ∞-category has an idempotent completion (Proposition 5.1.4.2). If f exhibits D as the idempotent completion of C and E is idempotent complete, composition with f gives an equivalence Fun(D, E) ≃ Fun(C, E) (Proposition 5.1.4.9). If C is stable, its idempotent completion is stable (HA Corollary 1.1.3.7).
hypotheses: Idempotent complete means that diagrams indexed by Idem have colimits (HTT §4.4.5, Corollary 4.4.5.15); no separate labelled ∞-categorical definition was located.

The universal property uses HTT Proposition 4.3.2.15 (Kan extensions, stage E3) and the stability statement uses HTT Lemma 5.4.2.4 on Ind-objects (stage E5:presentability); the atlas places both after E5:abstract (see gap).

Proposition 5.1.4.9: reduce to a full inclusion; every functor D → E is a left Kan extension of its restriction (Lemma 5.1.4.7, from Lemmas 5.1.4.3–5.1.4.6 and Theorem 4.1.3.1); extensions exist (Lemma 5.1.4.8, via P(D) and Proposition A.2.3.1); Proposition 4.3.2.15 makes f^* a trivial fibration.

nodes.title: Ind-completion: universal property, compact objects, stability and monoidal structure
nodes.statement: For C small and κ regular, Ind_κ(C) ⊆ P(C) consists of the presheaves classifying right fibrations with κ-filtered total space (HTT Definition 5.3.5.1); it is closed under κ-filtered colimits and consists of κ-filtered colimits of representables (Proposition 5.3.5.3, Corollary 5.3.5.4), and representables are κ-compact (Proposition 5.3.5.5). If D has small κ-filtered colimits, restriction along the Yoneda embedding j is an equivalence from κ-continuous functors Ind_κ(C) → D to Fun(C, D) (Proposition 5.3.5.10). A κ-continuous F with f = F ∘ j is fully faithful if f is fully faithful with κ-compact values, and is an equivalence iff moreover f generates D under κ-filtered colimits (Proposition 5.3.5.11). The κ-compact objects of Ind_κ(C) form an idempotent completion of C (Lemma 5.4.2.4). If C is small and stable, Ind_κ(C) is stable (HA Proposition 1.1.3.6); a stable C is presentable iff it has small coproducts, hC is locally small and there is a κ-compact generator (HA Corollary 1.4.4.2). A small symmetric monoidal C gives Ind(C) a symmetric monoidal structure for which j is symmetric monoidal and ⊗ preserves filtered colimits in each variable (HA Corollary 4.8.1.14).
hypotheses: C small, κ regular, D with κ-filtered colimits for the universal property.

No single source statement extending exact functors on C to colimit-preserving functors on Ind(C) was located; it must be assembled from HTT 5.3.5.10, 5.5.1.9, 5.4.2.4 and HA 1.1.4.1 (reader's inference).

nodes.title: Sifted colimits, P_Σ(C) and extension of functors along sifted colimits
nodes.statement: A simplicial set K is sifted if it is nonempty and the diagonal K → K × K is cofinal (HTT Definition 5.5.8.1); filtered simplicial sets are sifted and N(Δ)^op is sifted (Example 5.5.8.3, Lemma 5.5.8.4). For C small with finite coproducts, P_Σ(C) ⊆ P(C) is spanned by the presheaves preserving finite products (Definition 5.5.8.8); it is an accessible localization of P(C) closed under sifted colimits and compactly generated, and contains the representables (Proposition 5.5.8.10); X ∈ P_Σ(C) iff X is the colimit in P(C) of a simplicial object in Ind(C) (Lemma 5.5.8.14). If D has filtered colimits and geometric realizations, restriction gives an equivalence from sifted-colimit-preserving functors P_Σ(C) → D to Fun(C, D); such functors preserve sifted colimits; and if D has finite coproducts, g preserves small colimits iff g ∘ j preserves finite coproducts (Proposition 5.5.8.15). A functor out of an ∞-category with small colimits preserves sifted colimits iff it preserves filtered colimits and geometric realizations (Corollary 5.5.8.17).
hypotheses: C small with finite coproducts; D with filtered colimits and geometric realizations.

nodes.title: Animated commutative rings as finite-product-preserving functors on polynomial algebras
nodes.statement: For a commutative ring k let Poly_k be the category of polynomial k-algebras k[x₁, …, x_n]. An animated commutative k-algebra is a functor Poly_k^op → S that carries tensor products of polynomial algebras to products of spaces; these form CAlg^an_k ⊆ Fun(Poly_k^op, S), and for k = Z they are the animated commutative rings (Bhatt–Lurie, Absolute prismatic cohomology, Definition A.1). Ordinary commutative k-algebras embed fully faithfully as the discrete objects (Example A.2), and simplicial commutative k-algebras form a simplicial model category whose underlying ∞-category is CAlg^an_k (Remark A.4, citing HTT Corollary 5.5.9.3). For C with small sifted colimits, every F: Poly_k → C has an extension LF uniquely determined by commuting with sifted colimits (Proposition A.5, proved by reference to HTT Proposition 5.5.8.15), and LF preserves all small colimits iff F preserves finite coproducts (Remark A.7).
